hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

First, let me start with:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 18 and doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To help me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand more about his current situation.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

(For example, is he at school, college, university, or doing an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in college doing his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Since Alex is 18 and in approved education, he may still be eligible. However, you mentioned he doesn't live with you at the moment.

**Where is Alex currently living, and do you make any financial contributions towards his upkeep** (such as for food, clothes, accommodation, pocket money, or other expenses)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living with his dad, my ex-partner. As for financial contributions, I'm not really sure how to answer that - I do help out when I can, but I don't know if it counts or how much it adds up to exactly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me help clarify what counts as contributions. Contributions to your child's upkeep can include things like:

- Money for clothes, food, or pocket money
- Gifts or presents
- Financial contributions towards his accommodation
- Other regular or occasional financial support

These can be made weekly, monthly, or even as occasional lump sums.

**Can you give me a rough idea of how much you contribute in total over a typical month?** For reference, the current Child Benefit rate is £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child (which is about £102.40 per month). To continue receiving Child Benefit when a child lives elsewhere, you'd generally need to be contributing at least that amount or equivalent.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see what you mean. To be honest, I'm not entirely certain of the exact amount. Some months I might help with a bit for school supplies or give him some money when I see him, but I couldn't tell you for sure whether it adds up to that £25 a week or not. It varies quite a bit depending on what's going on.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about that. I understand the situation can be variable.

Let me ask a couple more questions to get a complete picture:

**Is Alex's dad currently claiming Child Benefit for him?** (Or do you know if anyone else is claiming it?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, his dad isn't claiming it. Nobody else is getting Child Benefit for Alex as far as I know.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to complete my assessment:

1. **Do you live in the UK?**

2. **Are you currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or are you asking about whether you could start/continue claiming it?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester. And no, I'm not currently claiming it. I'm asking about whether I could start claiming it for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

1. **Do you have the right to reside in the UK?** (For example, are you a British citizen, have settled status, or have another immigration status that gives you the right to reside here?)

2. **When you see Alex or are in contact with him, would you say you have a parental relationship and responsibility for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen, so I have the right to reside here. And yes, absolutely - I'm his mum and we have a good relationship. I still feel responsible for him even though he's living with his dad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Let me make sure I have the complete picture:

**One final question: Do you know if Alex is working at all, and if so, is he working 24 hours a week or more?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working. He's focused on his A-levels at college, so he's just studying full-time.

## Summary

Based on the information you've provided, I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex at this time. Here's why:

**What works in your favor:**
- Alex is 18 and in approved education (A-levels), so he meets the age criteria (children under 20 in approved education or training can qualify)
- You're a British citizen living in the UK
- You maintain a parental relationship with Alex
- Alex isn't working 24 hours or more per week
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for him

**The key uncertainty:**
Since Alex lives with his father rather than with you, you would need to be contributing **at least £25.60 per week (about £102.40 per month)** towards his upkeep to be eligible for Child Benefit. Contributions can include:
- Money for clothes, food, or pocket money
- School supplies
- Presents
- Financial help with accommodation
- Other regular or occasional financial support

You've mentioned you do help out with school supplies and give him money when you see him, but you're uncertain if this adds up to the required amount.

**What you could do:**
If you'd like to claim Child Benefit, I'd suggest tracking your contributions over a period to see if they meet or exceed £25.60 per week. If they do, you may be eligible to claim. You can also contact the Child Benefit Office directly to discuss your specific circumstances - they can provide guidance on whether your contributions would qualify.
